## Gate stamp

The triage author stamps the semantic call. This write-back is the round-1 ceiling.

P1 is that `packages/core/src/init-deposit/gitignore.ts` `CANONICAL_GITIGNORE_BASELINE` and `cmd/deft-install/setup.go` `canonicalGitignoreLines` list `.deft-cache/` and do not list `.deft-scratch/`, while `content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-phase-1-2.md` defaults one worktree per agent under `.deft-scratch/worktrees/<story-id>` and Phase 0 already checks gitignore coverage for `.deft-scratch/`. Maintainer `.gitignore` line 185 is a separate surface. Observed on Directive 0.119.5 consumer: `git check-ignore -q .deft-scratch` → NOT-ignored; `git add -A` warns on embedded git repository.

What this P1 is not:

- Not changing swarm default placement.
- Not the #4007 assist-scratch exemption itself.
- Not a recut of maintainer `.gitignore`.

Expected first ship is adding `.deft-scratch/` to both consumer baselines so `directive init` / `deft update` pick it up. Re-measured at `557873cf26f14fe17a289eea4a297584b4a1432e`.

audit-targets: none

Round 1, fresh critic. Open critique of #4841. Ceiling 5765365119 is the only in-envelope comment. Re-measured at `557873cf26f14fe17a289eea4a297584b4a1432e`.

## What holds

Adding `.deft-scratch/` to the two consumer baselines is the deposit path that already exists. A throwaway repo confirms the line stops the reported `git add`.

From that tree:

- `CANONICAL_GITIGNORE_BASELINE` has 41 lines. `canonicalGitignoreLines` has 48. Neither list contains `deft-scratch` or `temp/`. Every TypeScript line is in the Go list. The seven Go-only lines are legacy `vbrief/.eval/*` entries.
- Init (`init-deposit.ts`) and update (`refresh.ts`) both call `ensureInitGitignoreLines`. That function appends absent baseline lines. Doctor `checkGitignoreCoverage` compares the consumer file to the same TypeScript list and is advisory.
- The Go installer writes `canonicalGitignoreLines` in `EnsureGitignoreLines`. `TestCanonicalGitignoreContainsTypeScriptBaseline` requires each TypeScript line to be present in Go.
- This repo's `.gitignore` already lists `.deft-scratch/`, next to maintainer-only patterns (`docs/incidents/`, `handoff-*.md`). Init and update write the baseline into a consumer. They leave this repo's `.gitignore` where it is.
- `.claude/worktrees/` is already on both baselines so an agent worktree does not dirty the tree. `gitignore.test.ts` locks it with `toContain`. It is absent from `RUNTIME_WRITER_PATHS`.
- `defaultWorktree` always returns `<project>/.deft-scratch/worktrees/<story-id>`. No file under `packages/core/src/swarm` calls `git check-ignore`.

Throwaway repos, TypeScript baseline taken from that blob:

- With no `.deft-scratch/` rule, `git worktree add .deft-scratch/worktrees/story` (the worktree `.git` is a file) and `git add -A` print `warning: adding embedded git repository: .deft-scratch/worktrees/story` and stage `A  .deft-scratch/worktrees/story` (index mode 160000). A nested `git init` prints the same warning.
- With `.deft-scratch/` appended, `git check-ignore` matches the directory, the worktree, and a file inside it. `git add -A` stages `.gitignore` and leaves the worktree out.
- `git worktree add` into a directory that is already ignored exits 0. The parent `git status` stays empty.

## Inventory

| Need | Existing mechanism |
| --- | --- |
| Deposit the ignore on init and on update | `CANONICAL_GITIGNORE_BASELINE` through `ensureInitGitignoreLines` |
| Same line on the installer rail | `canonicalGitignoreLines` through `EnsureGitignoreLines`; TypeScript lines must be a subset |
| Keep an agent-worktree directory ignored | `.claude/worktrees/` on both baselines, plus `toContain` |
| Fail-closed coverage of `.deft/` local-cache writers | `RUNTIME_WRITER_PATHS_LOCAL_CACHE` and `runtime-writer-paths.json` |
| Remove a tracked path on purpose | `migrate --untrack-core`, scoped to `.deft/core` |
| Phase 0 gitignore check | Phase 0f skill prose. It asks before a gitignore edit. Launch does not call it |

## Findings

### 1. Refresh appends the line and leaves a committed gitlink in the index. `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence.** In a throwaway repo I committed the worktree gitlink, then committed `.deft-scratch/` in `.gitignore`. `git status --short` was empty. `git ls-files -s -- .deft-scratch` still showed mode `160000` for `.deft-scratch/worktrees/story`. `git check-ignore -v -- .deft-scratch/worktrees/story` exited 1. A new file `.deft-scratch/other/n.txt` stayed out of `git ls-files` on the next `git add -A`. The gitlink stayed. `refresh.ts` says `ensureInitGitignoreLines` writes `.gitignore` and leaves tracked paths tracked. The cached-remove verb on this surface is `migrate --untrack-core`, and it targets `.deft/core`.

**Failure mode.** A consumer who already ran `git add -A` has the gitlink on the branch. The next `directive update` appends the ignore. Status can look clean. `git ls-files` still contains `.deft-scratch/worktrees/<story>`. Clones still receive that gitlink.

**Disposition.** Bind append-only. Acceptance is an untracked path: once the line is present, `git add -A` does not stage `.deft-scratch/worktrees/<story>`. A path already in the index stays there until `git rm --cached` removes it. Keep that removal off `directive update`.

### 2. Lock the line the way `.claude/worktrees/` is locked. `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence.** `gitignore.test.ts` asserts `toContain(".claude/worktrees/")`. The runtime-writer manifest's local-cache entries are `.deft/` roots (`authz`, `metrics`, cache paths). `.deft-scratch` is absent. `TestCanonicalGitignoreContainsTypeScriptBaseline` fails when a TypeScript line is missing from Go. Removing one line from both lists leaves that test green. `TestRuntimeWritersCoveredByGoBaseline` stays green while the path is unregistered. Doctor compares the consumer file to the baseline, so it stays green when the baseline and the file move together.

**Failure mode.** The line lands on both baselines with no `toContain`. A later edit deletes it from both lists. Parity stays green, writer coverage stays green, and doctor stays green. `git add -A` stages the worktree gitlink again.

**Disposition.** Add `.deft-scratch/` beside `.claude/worktrees/` on both baselines, and add the same `toContain` on the TypeScript list. The existing subset test then requires the Go list to carry it. Init, update, and `EnsureGitignoreLines` all pick the line up from those two arrays.

**Road not taken.** Registering `.deft-scratch` on `RUNTIME_WRITER_PATHS_LOCAL_CACHE` and `runtime-writer-paths.json`. That registry is the local-cache versus tracked-provenance split for `.deft/` writer roots. `.claude/worktrees/` is the worktree-ignore precedent, and it lives outside the registry. Folding a nested-worktree root into local-cache would put it in the class whose throwaway test seeds probe files and expects a clean status. I would take the registry if `.deft-scratch` were a `.deft/` writer root, or if `.claude/worktrees/` were already in the manifest.

### 3. Leave `temp/` off this baseline change. `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence.** `ASSIST_SCRATCH_ROOT_PREFIXES` is `.deft-scratch/` and `temp/`. The allowlist matches the path prefix and does not call `git check-ignore`. Both prefixes are absent from both baselines. This repo's `.gitignore` ignores both. `reconcileGitignoreFile` appends a baseline line again after a consumer deletes it.

**Failure mode.** An implementer deposits both prefixes because the allowlist comment calls them gitignored. `temp/` is a generic directory name. A consumer who tracks `temp/` deletes the deposited line, and the next update appends it again. `.deft-scratch/` is a framework path and does not collide that way.

**Disposition.** The lean adds `.deft-scratch/` only. `temp/` stays off both baselines.

## Footnotes

- Phase 0f tells a greenfield swarm to look at `.gitignore` coverage for `.deft-scratch/` and to ask before editing it. `defaultWorktree` does not consult that step. Headless launch still creates the directory.
- Parent branch containing the rule, worker branch cut from the commit before it: parent `git status` stayed empty, and `git add -A` inside the worktree staged `.deft-scratch/subagent-status/a.json`. A branch that lacks the line can still commit in-worktree scratch.
- `git check-ignore -- .deft-scratch` misses the pattern `.deft-scratch/` while that directory is absent. The same command matches after `mkdir`. `git check-ignore -- .deft-scratch/` matches before the directory exists. The issue's command is the right check once the directory is there.
- The seven extra Go `vbrief/.eval/*` lines are already there. Update reads the TypeScript list. The installer reads the Go list. This change edits both.

## Chosen mechanism

Add the directory rule `.deft-scratch/` to both consumer baselines, same shape as `.claude/worktrees/`. Init and update append it. `git worktree add` under that ignored directory succeeds, so the swarm default path can stay. `git rm --cached` of an already indexed gitlink stays a separate operator step. `temp/` stays off the baseline. The runtime-writer registry stays the `.deft/` writer set.

Moving the default outside the repository is the other live option (the issue's workaround). It avoids the gitlink. I left it. The skill's reason for the in-repo path is to keep worktrees out of the projects folder, and `git worktree add` into the ignored directory exits 0. I would move the default if worktree creation under an ignored `.deft-scratch/` failed, or if parent `git status` still showed the worktree after the rule.

## Re-measured

Parsed both arrays from that blob. TypeScript has 41 lines. Go has 48. Every TypeScript line is in the Go list. The seven Go-only lines are legacy `vbrief/.eval/*` entries. Neither list contains `deft-scratch` or `temp/`. Both contain `.deft-cache/` and `.claude/worktrees/`.

- `directive init` calls `ensureInitGitignoreLines` (`packages/core/src/init-deposit/init-deposit.ts`). `directive update` calls it from `refresh.ts`. `reconcileGitignoreFile` appends each baseline line whose exact text is absent. It does not run `git rm --cached`.

- `TestCanonicalGitignoreContainsTypeScriptBaseline` fails when a quoted TypeScript line is missing from Go. `gitignore.test.ts` already locks `.claude/worktrees/` with `toContain`.

Throwaway repos, git 2.50.1, `core.excludesFile` pointed at `/dev/null`:

- No rule: `git worktree add .deft-scratch/worktrees/story`, then `git add -A`, warns `adding embedded git repository: .deft-scratch/worktrees/story` and stages mode `160000` plus `.deft-scratch/envelopes/a.json`.
- Rule `.deft-scratch/` present and those paths untracked: `git check-ignore -v` matches the directory, the worktree, and the envelope. `git add -A` stages only `.gitignore`.

A new untracked `.deft-scratch/other/n.txt` stays out of the index. `git check-ignore` on the tracked worktree path exits 1.

## Inventory

| Need | Existing mechanism |
| --- | --- |
| Deposit the line on init and on update | `CANONICAL_GITIGNORE_BASELINE` through `ensureInitGitignoreLines` |
| Same line on the installer | `canonicalGitignoreLines` through `EnsureGitignoreLines`; TypeScript lines must be a subset |
| Lock one consumer ignore line | `toContain(".claude/worktrees/")` in `gitignore.test.ts` |
| Warn when a consumer file lags the TypeScript list | `checkGitignoreCoverage` |
| Place the swarm worktree | `defaultWorktree` |
| Drop a tracked path on purpose | `migrate --untrack-core`, scoped to `.deft/core` |
| Triage bootstrap gitignore | Appends `.deft-cache/` and selective triage-cache lines. It is not this canonical baseline |

The remedy uses those deposit and lock mechanisms. It does not add a third writer.

## Footnotes

### 1. `git check-ignore -q .deft-scratch` misses a trailing-slash rule while the directory is absent. `footnote`

**Evidence.** With only `.deft-scratch/` in `.gitignore`, `git check-ignore -q .deft-scratch` exits 1 before `mkdir` and exits 0 after it. `git check-ignore -q .deft-scratch/` exits 0 either way.

The Stop 1 observation ran that command on a consumer with no rule. After the line exists, the same command still exits 1 until the directory is created. Swarm creates the directory before `git add -A`. The acceptance check named in the remedy is that add, and that add left the worktree unstaged.

### 2. A worktree checkout that lacks the line can still commit in-worktree scratch. `footnote`

**Evidence.** Worktree cut from the commit before `.deft-scratch/` existed: inside it, `git add -A` staged `.deft-scratch/subagent-status/a.json`. The same add on the commit that contains the line staged nothing.

`swarm:pre-dispatch` creates `<worktree>/.deft-scratch/subagent-status/`. That file sits in the worker checkout. The worker ignores it when the worker's `.gitignore` contains the line. A branch cut from a parent commit that does not yet contain the line can still commit it. The remedy's acceptance sentence is the line being present on the checkout that runs `git add`.

### 3. An indexed gitlink stays indexed. `footnote`

**Evidence.** After the gitlink and the envelope file were committed, adding `.deft-scratch/` left both in `git ls-files`. `refresh.ts` states that `ensureInitGitignoreLines` writes `.gitignore` and leaves tracked paths tracked. The cached-remove verb on this surface is `migrate --untrack-core`, and it targets `.deft/core`.

This matches the remedy's acceptance bullet: a path already in the index stays until `git rm --cached`, and that removal stays off `directive update`.

These footnotes leave the four Bound-remedy bullets as written.

metadata.issueBody:
## Summary

The swarm skill defaults agent worktrees to `.deft-scratch/worktrees/<story-id>`, describing that location as a "deterministic **ignored** scratch path". The framework-generated `.gitignore` does not ignore `.deft-scratch/`, so the default location is tracked.

## Evidence

`.gitignore` in a consumer project, framework-generated (its own header says so):

```
# Deft framework: ignore local-only caches and scratch directories
# Hybrid deposit (#1942): reconstituted by `directive init` like node_modules.
.deft-cache/
.deft/cache/
.deft/.cli/
...
.deft/core/
```

`.deft-cache/` is listed. `.deft-scratch/` is not. Meanwhile `skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-phase-1-2.md:51`:

> ! One worktree per agent under deterministic ignored scratch paths by default: `.deft-scratch/worktrees/<story-id>`.

```
$ git check-ignore -q .deft-scratch && echo ignored || echo NOT-ignored
NOT-ignored
```

## Consequence

A `git add -A` in a project that has used the swarm default stages the worktrees:

```
warning: adding embedded git repository: .deft-scratch/worktrees/<name>
hint: You've added another git repository inside your current repository.
```

It also stages any other scratch written there — in this project, design-critique envelopes. An agent following the swarm skill's own default produces a repository state that the next ordinary `git add -A` corrupts.

Related: `.deft-scratch/` is also the path the #4007 write-fence message offers as its disposable-notes exemption, which is a second reason it should be reliably ignored.

## Expected

`directive init` / `deft update` should include `.deft-scratch/` in the generated `.gitignore`, alongside `.deft-cache/`. Existing projects would pick it up on the next deposit refresh.

## Workaround

Place swarm worktrees in sibling directories outside the repository instead of the documented default.

## Environment

Directive 0.119.5, consumer project, macOS. Observed while running a two-story swarm cohort.
